decision_reason: ChebTools is a documented C++11/Python library for Chebyshev expansions, roots, derivatives, and related numerical operations. Its NIST authorship is supported by NIST's publication record and JOSS paper; the exact repository has build/install/API examples and has been used in NIST thermophysical-property research. The current root license is standard MIT, and the first checked grant-bearing source tree with that standard MIT license is the February 2018 commit.

government_provenance.note: NIST's publication page identifies the exact software and its authors; the JOSS paper specifies Ian Bell and Bradley Alpert at NIST Boulder and Lucas Bouck at George Mason, and the exact NIST repository is the paper's software link.

public_source.note: The repository publicly exposes C++11 and Python source, tests, build/install instructions, examples, and a LICENSE without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The February 6, 2018 license commit removes earlier Terms of Use and contains the standard MIT grant/disclaimer with NIST copyright notice; current LICENSE retains that standard MIT text. This is distinct from the earlier custom version that stated U.S.-only noncopyrightability. Unmodified Eigen is a separate third-party dependency under its own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The peer-reviewed JOSS paper describes the exact ChebTools library and links the repository; NIST publications document its use in thermodynamic mixture rootfinding. The README gives concrete Python API usage, CMake/Python installation, and tests.

product_identity: ChebTools, a C++11 library with Python bindings for constructing/evaluating Chebyshev polynomial expansions, rootfinding, differentiation, integration, and related numerics; not the separate Chebfun project
agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), with NIST authors Ian H. Bell and Bradley K. Alpert; coauthor Lucas Bouck affiliated with George Mason University
geography: United States federal research; NIST, Boulder, Colorado
license: Standard MIT for ChebTools repository-authored software from the 2018-02-06 license revision onward. Eigen is an unmodified separate dependency with its own license. First public code under this verified standard-MIT version is evidenced by the 2018 source/license commit.
status_note: NIST's JOSS paper was published 2018-02-12 and the source repository had working installation/API instructions by the first eligible standard-MIT grant commit on 2018-02-06. Earlier repository license history includes a custom Terms of Use/modified-MIT phase; do not use its 2017 license date. Maintained: the repository shows substantive packaging/dependency updates through 2025-07-02 and a 2024-01 v1.12.0 release. Catalog only ChebTools-authored library code; do not transfer Eigen or wrapper/runtime terms.

eligible_license.note: The visible root has README, CHANGELOG, metadata, attributes, files, recipes, and templates but no LICENSE/COPYING file or explicit software grant. The NIST inventory's generic license URL is not a repository-scoped grant.

product_identity: Incomplete Chef cookbook skeleton for an httpd recipe; exact intended NIST product/use not established
agency: NIST relationship unresolved for this exact repository; no attributable sponsoring office found
geography: United States; specific government sponsor not established

decision_reason: ChemNLP is a documented NIST materials-chemistry NLP library with installable Python package, scholarly validation, and a live NIST JARVIS web application linked by the README. Hold under the strict license gate: the exact LICENSE.rst is the older custom NIST notice (U.S.-only statutory public domain plus a non-exclusive foreign permission and explicit foreign-copyright reservation), not OSI-approved NIST-Software or a clear worldwide public-domain dedication. No eligible first licensed-source year is asserted until that grant is cleared.

government_provenance.note: NIST's official staff profile identifies JARVIS-ChemNLP and links the exact GitHub repository; the 2023 journal article lists NIST Material Measurement Laboratory affiliation for the lead author and identifies this exact code/webapp.

public_source.note: The repository publicly exposes Python package source, tests, example workflows, setup metadata, and the license notice without credentials; README documents pip and source installation.

eligible_license.note: The exact Terms of Use says NIST employee work is not copyrightable in the United States, says software may be subject to foreign copyright, and separately grants non-exclusive foreign permissions subject to notice. This is not the current OSI NIST-Software text (which requires explicit NIST acknowledgement and different terms), nor a clear worldwide public-domain dedication.

primary_evidence.note: The peer-reviewed 2023 paper identifies the exact ChemNLP library, its workflows, datasets, and both repository and NIST web app. The NIST JARVIS homepage and staff profile currently link the exact ChemNLP deployment; README and PyPI metadata provide install and usage examples.

product_identity: ChemNLP, a Python library and JARVIS web application for chemical-literature processing, text classification/clustering, named entity extraction, and materials-chemistry text mining; a JARVIS component but independently documented
agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Material Measurement Laboratory; NIST JARVIS team
geography: United States federal research; NIST, Gaithersburg, Maryland
license: Unresolved custom NIST Terms of Use (U.S.-only public-domain statement plus foreign-rights reservation and conditional non-exclusive permission); not OSI NIST-Software. Python, ML, and data dependencies remain separately licensed.
status_note: The 2023 paper and current JARVIS pages establish exact product use/distribution; those dates do not establish an eligible worldwide grant. Hold pending an exact OSI-approved code license or authoritative confirmation that the newer NIST-Software license applies to this exact source. Keep scoped to ChemNLP, not the entire JARVIS platform.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains an MIT license attributed to Daniel Wheeler, but it applies only to files in this redirect repository; it cannot be transferred to the separate PFHub site or any external code.

primary_evidence.note: README says 'Dummy repository for redirecting to https://pages.nist.gov/pfhub'. No NIST release, code use, or software support is established for this assigned URL as an independent product.

product_identity: NIST GitHub redirect placeholder pointing to the Phase Field Community Hub (PFHub); no software implementation in this repository
agency: NIST-associated redirect to PFHub only; government sponsorship of code in this repository is not established
geography: United States; linked NIST-hosted PFHub website, no standalone product site for this repo

status_note: The assigned URL is a stub redirect, not the source for PFHub. Do not move this MIT notice or NIST-hosted Pages URL to an unassigned successor repository; review the actual canonical product source separately if assigned.

decision_reason: This repository is a CHIPS combined/hybrid metrology project description with figures and simple webpage assets, not the promised software suite itself. The README describes planned expansions to separate existing NexusLIMS and WIPP products and future tools, but this repository has no project-specific source license, packaged release, install/use guidance, or distributable product identity.

government_provenance.note: The exact README identifies the CHIPS Combined and Hybrid Metrology effort and names a cross-division NIST project team, including Office of Data and Informatics, Software and Systems Division, Microsystems and Nanotechnology Division, and Statistical Engineering Division.

public_source.note: The public tree contains the project-description README, three figures, script.js, and styles.css; it does not contain the identified NexusLIMS/WIPP software or a separate hybrid-metrology application source.

eligible_license.note: No LICENSE/COPYING grant is present in the visible repository root. The generic NIST inventory license label is not evidence that the description/web assets or separately named NexusLIMS/WIPP components share an eligible grant.

primary_evidence.note: The README describes a project plan and future outcomes ('will be made available', 'create and release') while separately naming NexusLIMS and WIPP as existing NIST resources to be expanded. It does not document a versioned software release, installation, user instructions, or exact code use for this repo.

product_identity: CHIPS combined and hybrid metrology project-description/site-assets repository; future suite proposal, not NexusLIMS, WIPP, or a released hybrid-metrology software product
agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), cross-divisional CHIPS Metrology project team named in the README

license: No repository-level software license found; no product-wide license inference for NexusLIMS or WIPP, which are separate products
status_note: Reject this planning/description repository as a software entry. Its README states that tools are planned, while named NexusLIMS/WIPP software are separate existing resources whose provenance and grants must be reviewed in their own canonical repositories.
